messages:
maya: FYI, after the kernel + batching scheduler change rolled at 03:20 UTC we're seeing a sharp erosion in lead-in (prefix) cache hit rate for long-context workloads. metrics show the 0-64 token prefix hit dropping from ~78% -> ~21% on the main inference pool.
ranjit: ugh. which rollout exactly? kernel variant + new batcher heuristics?
maya: yes — fused-attn-v2 kernel + 'latency-first' batching window (batcher_v2). deploy-bot: deployed fused-attn-v2 to pool=prod-highmem at 03:19:47 UTC.
sasha: can you paste the query and a small timeseries?
maya: sure -- small snippet from metrics DB:
```
-- per-minute prefix cache hit rate (avg)
SELECT time, avg(prefix_hit) FROM inference.metrics
WHERE pool='prod-highmem' AND model='redwood-3b' AND time > now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY time ORDER BY time;
```
maya: results (abridged):
03:00 0.775
03:10 0.772
03:19 0.768  <-- pre-rollout
03:21 0.319
03:25 0.241
03:30 0.212

devon: did we change key normalization or salt? that would explain misses even if cache is warmed.
maya: I checked binary diffs for the runtime flags we flipped: no explicit key-salt change, but the kernel introduced a different padding/truncation ordering for token ids when computing the context fingerprint. logs show fingerprint keys differing by a trailing 0x00 in many samples.
ranjit: that sounds like a canonicalization mismatch. can you show an example key pair (pre vs post) from the runtime debug logs?
maya: pasted a few lines from debug dump (sanitized):
```
pre_fingerprint: f2a1b3c4d5e6:len=128:pad=right
post_fingerprint: f2a1b3c4d5e6:len=128:pad=right:tile=4b
```
maya: notice the extra ":tile=4b" suffix after fused-attn-v2 path.
sasha: hmm that suffix is the kernel affinity tag we added to help scheduler pick matmul tiling — it ended up being incorporated into the cache key mistakenly.
ranjit: confirm: cache key includes the kernel-affinity string? if so, different kernel variants will always miss each others' entries.
maya: yes. prefix cache stores keys as "model:context_hash:kernel_meta" and the kernel_meta field is now variant-specific. that's the regression.
devon: ok urgent fix options: 1) strip kernel affinity from cache key (best long term), 2) normalize keys for compatibility (hotpatch), 3) rollback kernel on prod.
ranjit: quick mitigation: add compatibility layer where lookup tries both variant-specific and variant-agnostic keys for N minutes. cheap to hotpatch.
perf-bot: alert: average token latency increased 18% and cost per request up ~12% since 03:20 UTC.
sasha: agree with ranjit — implement dual-lookup first then change key generation. I can draft the patch.
maya: I pushed a branch with the dual-lookup impl and small perf guard to avoid extra lookups for warm pools. here's the defensive diff (concept):
```
if cache_lookup(key_with_kernel) -> hit: return
else if cache_lookup(key_without_kernel) -> insert(key_with_kernel, value); return
```
ranjit: ok test on canary pool (prod-canary) and measure prefix hit recovery.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy to prod-canary at 03:42 UTC (maya/dual-lookup-hotfix).
maya: canary metrics after 5m: prefix hit recovered to 74% on canary. latency down ~10% vs rollout.
ranjit: good. schedule 30m progressive rollout to other pools with monitoring guard.
sasha: follow-up: we should also decouple cache key from kernel metadata; keys must only reflect semantic context (model + tokenization + requested params). kernel affinity belongs to runtime routing metadata. I'll open a follow-up RFC.
devon: also verify this doesn't mask other issues — if kernel variant legitimately changes output semantics we need separate cache buckets per-semantic-variant.
maya: agreed. for now dual-lookup + canonicalization patch goes to prod in 15m. putting notes into /eng-runtime channel and I'll file a postmortem once we stabilize. :thumbsup:
ranjit: thanks — great catch. can you annotate the rollout with the exact commit sha and file the RFC link?
maya: will do. commit: 7b9d4f2, canary rollout started 03:42, full rollout at 03:58 after positive canary.
perf-bot: resolved: prefix cache hit alarm cleared at 04:05 UTC on prod-highmem.
maya: closing the thread for now, will follow up with a short postmortem and the RFC.
